title: Chapter 2944 - 174: Money Rat
content:
Chapter 2944: Chapter 174: Money Rat

Mo Hua could feel that these demon creatures resembling "Money Rats" were currently crawling beside him, gnawing at his flesh, and even through his flesh, they were gnawing at his Divine Thought, causing some damage to his Dao body.

At the same time, their mouths seemed to be mixed with venom.

This venom, somehow, seeped into his Sea of Consciousness, softened the Divine Thought, and amplified the pain.

It was only then that Mo Hua realized why inscribing the Taotie Pattern was so painful—not just because of the issues with the Taotie Formation itself.

But also because these "Money Rats" were harming him.

They gnaw at him, making his Divine Thought "poisoned." The overlap of poison and pain, under their twofold effect, the savage pain of Taotie’s devouring would escalate to a level that ordinary cultivators simply could not endure.

During the process of molding the Life Formation, once the pain exceeds the limits of what the Divine Sense can endure, it can drive one mad and certainly lead to grave mistakes.

Minor mistakes can distort the Formation Patterns, making all efforts futile.

Major mistakes can damage the bones, scatter the Vital Energy, and make the Great Dao hopeless.

In more severe cases, the Life Formation could self-destruct, resulting in death on the spot.

Were it not for Mo Hua’s possession of strong "Divinity," and the coldness of the "Non-Human" brought by the Divinity, and his almost cruel indifference to himself... the consequences would be unimaginable.

It would have been impossible for him to inscribe the Twelve Meridians Taotie Lifebound Spirit Formation.

Even now, though he successfully inscribed the Life Formation, to suppress the pain, he was forced to utilize too much "Divinity."

The "Divinity" has greatly exceeded the limit, so much so that now, he’s not even sure how much humanity he has left in him.

Anger surged in Mo Hua’s heart.

It was an anger that was almost devoid of "humanity," not interfering with rationality, cold anger.

It was pure "Divine Fury."

Sensing this "Divine Fury," the insidious "Money Rats" that were stealing bites from Mo Hua’s Dao body all paused, their eyes filled with ferocity, their fangs elongated, each becoming hideous and grotesque, baring their teeth and claws at Mo Hua, and even intensified their "gnawing."

Mo Hua’s eyes flashed with golden light, and the Divine Sword shattered reality.

Where the sword light reached, the divine power burned like fire, these grotesque "Money Rats" were crushed into powder, violently meeting their demise.

In the Divine Way and Heavenly Mechanism Causality, these "tricks of the ghosts," sinister rodents, naturally weren’t a match for Mo Hua.

If he didn’t notice, then so be it.

Now that he knows, just one look at them, they must die.

After exterminating the Money Rats, Mo Hua fell into contemplation.

"These Money Rats... what are they..."

"Is someone... harming me?"

Mo Hua’s gaze slightly darkened.

This cave was selected casually in his Divine Blessing campaign, and had undergone extensive calculations, concealing the heavenly secret, closing off cause and effect, logically, no other person should know.

Yet to his surprise, these "Money Rats" still managed to find him.

In the most crucial moment of "inscribing the Life Formation," these Money Rats were undermining his foundation, trying to kill him...

Who on earth... has this ability to track his cause and effect, pinpoint his location?

Who also possesses the means to deliver these "Money Rats," appearing silently, beside him?

How could they seize the exact moment he is "inscribing the Life Formation," during the internal and external peril intertwining period, his alertness lowered, which is almost the most "fragile" moment...

"Money Rats..."

Mo Hua’s gaze gradually turned dangerous.

A moment later, he looked around, his eyes possessing the vision of a deity.

The Money Rats were all killed, the Cause and Effect Line "self-ignited" and severed, the heavenly secret means contained within were extremely skilled.

This is also the only way that can "harm" him.

Besides that, there is no other danger within the cave.

Only then did Mo Hua manipulate the formation tools, unlocked the shackles, and pulled out the bloody needles from his body.

On his fair skin, the flesh turned outward, the pain intense.

But having endured more violent, deeper, torturous, even long-lasting to an endless inscribing of Life Formation pain, these pure physical pains were already nothing.

Mo Hua slowly stood up, condensed Water Qi, washed away the blood filth on his body, took out some medicinal juice, and applied it to his skin.

The scars on the outer skin were being slowly repaired.

And inside him, the "post-surgical" trauma left behind by bone carving, along with the operation of his Life Formation, nurtured by the Wood Revitalization Formation, was automatically healing.

Mo Hua, thin and fair, with a Heavenly People-like physique, was recovering, little by little, as before.

Mo Hua donned Divine Blessing’s robe again, transforming into the handsome and solemn Divine Blessing Lord.

Meanwhile, there was a deep, profound majesty gathered in his golden eyes.

Subsequently, Mo Hua stowed away all the tools used for inscribing the Life Formation into his Storage Ring.

Those that couldn’t be stowed were completely burned away using the Fireball Technique, leaving no trace or cause and effect.

After finishing all this, Mo Hua slowly walked out of the cave.

Outside the cave, a giant coffin was parked at the entrance.

The "Undying General" Sishen was guarding the entrance.

Besides that, Lugu, Dan Zhu, and the Big Tiger were also guarding nearby.

Seeing Mo Hua come out, the faces of Dan Zhu and others lit with joy, looking at Mo Hua, but upon seeing Mo Hua, their faces all became solemn.

Mo Hua’s aura began to change.

His cultivation advanced further, reaching Foundation Establishment Peak, with some signs of transforming towards the Golden Core.

Meanwhile, Mo Hua’s presence became stronger.

It was an aura uniquely belonging to the noble "deity," lofty, unobtrusive, divine charm reserved, yet extremely domineering.
